title: Deep merge for the config loader
prompt:
Our config loader shallow-merges with Object.assign, so an override like { db: { pool: 20 } } wipes out every other db setting. Please add src/merge.ts exporting two functions, and switch loadConfig in src/config.ts to use deepMerge (its signature stays the same).

deepMerge(target, ...sources) returns a new object: target with each source merged over it, left to right. deepMergeWith(options, target, ...sources) is the same with options; the only option is arrays: "replace" (the default) or "concat".

Rules:
- Only plain objects are merged: objects whose prototype is Object.prototype or null. When both sides of a key are plain objects, they merge recursively. Otherwise the source value replaces the target value.
- Plain objects in the result are ordinary objects (prototype Object.prototype) and always new objects (even ones that came from only one input), so changing the result never changes an input, and no input is mutated.
- Arrays: with "replace" the source array replaces the target value; with "concat", when both values are arrays the result is a new array with the target's items then the source's. Either way the result holds a new array whose items are the same values (not copied).
- Anything else (Date, Map, class instances, functions) is used as-is, by reference.
- A source property whose value is undefined is ignored entirely: it neither overwrites nor adds the key. null is a normal value.
- Only own enumerable string keys are read. The keys "__proto__", "constructor" and "prototype" are skipped at every depth.
- Key order: the target's keys first, then new keys in the order the sources introduce them.
- null or undefined sources are skipped. A target that is not a plain object, or a source that is neither a plain object nor null/undefined, throws a TypeError. An arrays option other than "replace" or "concat" throws a RangeError.
acceptance: Recursive merge of plain objects incl. null-prototype; new objects throughout and inputs untouched; replace vs concat arrays with new arrays sharing items; Dates/class instances/functions by reference; undefined ignored, null kept; dangerous keys skipped at depth (incl. JSON.parse('{"__proto__":...}')); key order; null/undefined sources skipped; TypeError/RangeError cases; loadConfig deep-merges.
difficulty_rationale: Several interacting rules (plain-object test, copying, arrays option, undefined, dangerous keys, ordering) and a caller to update.
